rules.description: The foundational ink of the design, heavily utilizing opacity to create a comprehensive scale for text, borders, and shadows.
when_to_use: Primary and secondary typography across all headings, body text, and menus
Subtle borders on cards, videos, and dropdowns (using low opacity)
Drop shadows on interactive components and bento boxes

rules.description: The dominant surface color that defines the clean, document-like feel, accompanied by subtle off-white and pastel shades for grouping.
when_to_use: Global page background and sticky navigation panel
Text and icon color on primary CTA buttons
Off-white backgrounds for bento box headers and the bottom endcap section
Pale color-tinted backgrounds (blue, red, yellow) for product feature cards

rules.description: A specific muted gray used to visually de-emphasize continuous background information.
when_to_use: Text color for the statistics within the scrolling marquee section

rules.description: A soft, low-contrast gray specifically paired with marquee text.
when_to_use: Icon fills accompanying the statistics in the scrolling marquee section

rules.description: The sole structural accent color, used exclusively to highlight interactive elements, conversions, and key feature markers.
when_to_use: Primary 'Get Notion free' CTA button backgrounds
Text color for 'Request a demo' secondary buttons
Inline text links with directional arrows
Filled graphic icons in the agent and feature prompt sections

insights: Opacity-driven hierarchy: Instead of a large palette of solid grays, the design primarily relies on pure black with varying alpha channels to handle typographic hierarchy, borders, disabled states, and shadows.
Document-first aesthetic: The heavy reliance on white surfaces and crisp black ink reinforces the product's identity as a text-focused workspace and system of record.

Restrained accentuation: By committing almost entirely to a monochrome foundation, the single blue accent color stands out sharply, creating an obvious visual path for user conversion and feature discovery.
